summary: The password reset confirm endpoint accepted a token that should already be used; a regression of single-use enforcement is the most likely explanation.

findings.summary: Reused reset token was not rejected
findings.observed_behavior: The confirm request with an already-used token did not return 400 token_used.
findings.expected_behavior: The confirm endpoint rejects a used token with 400 and error 'token_used'; the first new password keeps working.

probable_root_cause.description: Likely a regression of the single-use check: the used flag may not be persisted or checked in the confirm transaction.
probable_root_cause.reasoning: The observed response contradicts the documented contract, and BUG-1042 describes the same symptom.

alternative_causes.description: Possibly test data drift: the fixture token may have been regenerated and never used.

evidence.interpretation: The request did not produce the expected rejection.
Execution details of the failing run.
Server logs show the token check was skipped.

unknowns: Server logs for the confirm request are not available
Whether the fixture token had actually been used before this run
findings.severity_rationale: A reusable reset token lets anyone holding an old link take over the account.
reproduction_steps: Complete a password reset with a token
POST /api/v2/password-reset/confirm again with the same token and a new password
recommended_next_investigation: Check whether password_reset_tokens.used_at is set for the fixture token
Inspect the confirm handler for the used_at check introduced by BUG-1042
